in_arabic.name: أزهري
in_arabic.meaning: مشتق من اسم الله عز وجل، يعني الشخص الذي يتصف بالعزة والجلال
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي، مشتق من اسم الله عز وجل 'العزيز' و'الجواد'، يعني الشخص الذي يتصف بالعزة والجلال، ويتميز بالكرم والسخاء، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم عدة مرات في سياق وصفه تعالى بالعزة والقدرة

in_urdu.name: ازہاری
in_urdu.meaning: اللہ کے نام سے ماخوذ، عزت و جلال کا حامل
in_urdu.long_meaning: عربی मूल کا مذکر علم، اللہ کے نام 'العزيز' و 'الجواد' سے ماخوذ، جس کا مطلب ہے عزت و جلال کا حامل، کرم و سخاء کا مظہر، قرآن کریم میں کئی بار اس کی صفات عزت و قدرت کے ساتھ ذکر کی گئی ہیں، اسلامی تقویم میں اس نام کی اہمیت ہے

in_hindi.name: अज़हरी
in_hindi.meaning: भगवान के नाम से लिया गया, सम्मान और महिमा का स्वामी
in_hindi.long_meaning: अरबी मूल का पुल्लिंग नाम, भगवान के नाम 'العزيز' और 'الجواد' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है सम्मान और महिमा का स्वामी, उदारता और سخاء का प्रतीक, कुरआन में कई बार इसकी विशेषताएं सम्मान और शक्ति के साथ वर्णित की गई हैं, इस्लामी परंपरा में इस नाम का महत्व है

in_english.name: Azhari
in_english.meaning: Derived from Allah's name, means the one who possesses glory and majesty
in_english.long_meaning: A masculine given name of Arabic origin, derived from Allah's names 'العزيز' (al-Azīz) and 'الجواد' (al-Jawād), meaning the one who possesses glory and majesty, characterized by generosity and munificence, mentioned several times in the Quran in the context of describing Allah's attributes of glory and power, holds significant spiritual and cultural importance in Islamic tradition

data.cultural_impact: The name Azhari signifies intelligence, wisdom, and knowledge. In various Islamic societies and communities, the name is often associated with scholars, intellectuals, and thinkers. It carries a sense of uniqueness and pride, as the person carrying this name is considered to be a bearer of valuable knowledge and understanding within their community and beyond.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Azhari holds deeper significance in the context of Islamic teachings. In the Quran, Allah (swt) refers to those who are guided and possess knowledge as 'azhara'. By bestowing this name upon someone, the parents or guardians are expressing the hope that the child shall grow up to be a wise and knowledgeable individual in search of truth and knowledge. The name encourages the pursuit of knowledge, which is an essential pillar of the Islamic faith and a primary means for individuals to draw closer to Allah. Moreover, the name serves as a reminder of the virtue of intellect, which Allah highly values and advocates for in the Quran. In essence, the name Azhari inspires the individual to strive for knowledge and wisdom, both secular and spiritual, throughout their life, ultimately leading them towards greater closeness to Allah.
